roadmap.tag_renumbering: DISTILL tagged scenarios with a 00/01..05-xx scheme (27 sub-steps). This roadmap regroups them into 8 steps (01-01..01-04, 02-01..02-04); every #[ignore = "DELIVER <step>: ..."] reason was rewritten to the new step id (description text unchanged). Old -> new: 00 + 01-01/01-02/01-03 -> 01-01; 01-04/01-05/03-01/03-03 -> 01-02; 03-02/03-06/02-03/02-04/04-07/04-08 -> 01-03; 02-01/02-02/02-05/02-08/03-04 -> 01-04; 02-06/02-07/02-09/02-10 -> 02-01; 02-11/03-05 -> 02-02; 04-01..04-06/04-09/04-10 -> 02-03; 05-01..05-05 -> 02-04. The enablement order in distill/test-scenarios.md §'DELIVER enablement order' is superseded by this file.
global_rules: Keep main green: every step is independently committable; scenarios of later steps stay #[ignore]. Remove one ignore at a time, see it RED for the right reason, then GREEN.

After any change to a shared crate (ports, lexicon, appview-domain, test-support, tests/acceptance/support) run the dependent suites NARROWLY (cargo test -p <crate> / cargo test -p cli --test <target>), never the whole workspace on the host; CI verifies the full suite.
Trunk-based: commit to main, no PRs. Workflow (.github/workflows) changes are pushed over SSH.

phases.name: Per-DID PDS resolution: walking skeleton, fallback-as-relay, failure isolation
phases.description: The indexer resolves every configured repo DID to its own PDS each pass, binds listed records to the requested repo, classifies origin only through ListingSource (the fallback is always relay origin), and isolates per-DID resolution/listing failures as structured skips. Sequential fan-out is acceptable in this phase; bounds, deadlines and the SSRF guard arrive in phase 02.

steps.name: Harness migration + walking skeleton: resolve each DID to its own PDS every pass
steps.description: First, migrate the EXISTING indexer harness so later config hardening cannot break it: FakeIngestServer derives bare repo DIDs (no '#fragment') for OPENLORE_INDEXER_REPO_DIDS and at:// URIs, and every existing indexer spawner sets OPENLORE_INDEXER_PLC_ENDPOINT to a hermetic local directory that 404s (never the live plc.directory) plus OPENLORE_INDEXER_ALLOW_LOOPBACK_HTTP=1 (already set, inert). With PLC 404ing, every legacy DID routes through the fallback (the old OPENLORE_INDEXER_SOURCE_URL), reproducing today's behaviour; RD-7 in review_app_self_attested_readers becomes 'Priya unresolvable -> read via fallback = relay -> refused'. Then land the walking skeleton: new pure module appview_domain::ingest_pass (ListingSource{OwnPds(endpoint),Fallback}, ResolutionFailure, ListingPlan, plan_listing, origin_of, PassSummary/summarize), IdentityLookupPort::resolve_pds default method + IdentityLookup override (DID document only, pure pds_endpoint_of requiring id == did), and run.rs ingest reworked into a per-DID fetch phase (resolve every pass, never cached) + gate phase, emitting pass_summary as the last stdout event. IndexerWiring.source_url becomes fallback: Option<FallbackUrl>, built only in the new config.rs (minimal parse_config: repo DIDs, fallback, PLC endpoint — no new refusals yet).
criteria: Existing suites indexer_ingest, appview_core, appview_search, search_hide_retracted, review_app_self_attested_readers and the viewer search suites pass unchanged in assertions (RD-7 reworded only as specified) with bare DIDs and a hermetic local directory; no test contacts plc.directory
Maria finds Priya's self-attested claim published on Priya's own PDS, attributed to Priya's bare DID with author-PDS origin (WS-1)
Authors on three different PDSes are all indexed in one pass and the pass summary counts own=3, fallback=0, skipped=0 (WS-2)
An author who moved PDS between passes is listed from the new PDS on the next pass; nothing is cached across passes (IPF-01)
Property: origin_of(OwnPds(e), f) is AuthorPds iff f == e (CORE-2)

ORDER INSIDE THE STEP: (1) harness migration alone, run the existing suites narrowly, commit green; (2) then the skeleton. Do the migration as its own commit so a regression is attributable. DISTILL hand-off item 1: FakeIngestServer (tests/acceptance/support/mod.rs ~L5551) currently builds DIDs from the app-signed author 'did:plc:priya-test#org.openlore.application'; derive the bare repo DID for REPO_DIDS and at:// URIs while the record's author/app identity keeps its fragment. Add (or reuse from FakeAtprotoNetwork) a hermetic 404 directory and set OPENLORE_INDEXER_PLC_ENDPOINT in all 5 spawn sites (support/mod.rs x4, review_app_self_attested_readers.rs). Shared harness change => run each dependent suite narrowly: indexer_ingest, appview_core, appview_search, search_hide_retracted, review_app_self_attested_readers, viewer_* search targets.
SKELETON: pure core in appview-domain (no tokio, no reqwest — the existing check_arch pure-core arm must stay green). origin_of(Fallback, _) returns Relay with no URL input on that arm (subtype layer of Earned Trust). Move run.rs decoded_records_of -> appview_domain::ingest_pass::records_of (foreign count lands in 01-02); delete run.rs origin_for once origin_of is wired. resolve_pds is a read-only DID-document fetch with NO handle back-check; pds_endpoint_of(did, &doc) is pure and gets a property test (id mismatch and missing #atproto_pds are errors). Sequential per-DID loop is fine here; bounded fan-out is 02-01. pass_summary must be the LAST stdout event. Contract shape of run.rs ingest: bounded-change (mutation set = index.duckdb indexed_claims upserts + stdout/stderr). Upsert failure stays fatal (exit 2). Other 01-xx..02-xx scenarios remain #[ignore].

steps.name: Repo binding and origin only via ListingSource: the fallback is always relay
steps.description: records_of keeps only records of the requested repo and counts foreign ones; tampered self-attested records are still refused by the CID == rkey gate when read from the author's own PDS. plan_listing yields Fallback for an unresolvable DID when a fallback is configured; anything read via the fallback is relay origin, even when the fallback URL equals someone's resolved PDS (no URL comparison, OQ-IPF-3). A fallback read emits source_fallback. New xtask rule indexer_origin_only_via_listing_source bans RecordOrigin::of / RecordOrigin::AuthorPds in non-test indexer sources, with a vacuity guard.
criteria: Records of another repo served by an author's PDS are never attributed to the requested author and are counted as foreign_repo (IPF-02)
A tampered self-attested record is refused (cid_mismatch) even when read from the author's own PDS (IPF-03)
An unresolvable author's app-signed claims are indexed through the fallback with relay origin and a source_fallback event (IPF-04)
A fallback that is somebody's own PDS never vouches for self-attested claims read through it (IPF-06)
Property: records_of keeps every own record and counts every foreign one (CORE-10); origin_of(Fallback, any) == Relay (CORE-1)

steps.name: Resolution failures and fallback eligibility (incl. NFR-3 single-source regression)
steps.description: Every DID-document failure class (not found, directory 5xx, id mismatch, no PDS service, unresolvable did:web) maps to a ResolutionFailure; plan_listing turns it into Fallback when a fallback is configured, otherwise Skip(DidUnresolvable) emitted as source_skipped without a PDS address. A resolved DID has no code path to the fallback. did:web DIDs are accepted. A single-source deployment (every author on the old source URL, which is also the fallback) indexes exactly what it did before, with and without the directory reachable.
criteria: A resolvable author is never read from the fallback (IPF-05); property: plan_listing never sends a resolved DID to the fallback (CORE-3)
A did:web author whose web host is down is read through the fallback (IPF-09)
An unresolvable author with no fallback is skipped with reason did_unresolvable, fallback_used false and no pds_url, while others are indexed (IPF-12)
Each DID-document failure (not found, directory error, different id, no PDS) skips that author as did_unresolvable and lists nothing on its host (IPF-13)

steps.name: Per-DID fault isolation: listing failures skip one author, never abort or delete
steps.description: Replace the exit-2 abort on a source failure with per-DID isolation: classify_fetch_failure maps every FetchFailure (unreachable, 5xx, 429, 404, non-JSON, redirect, fallback failure) to exactly one SkipReason; the listing adapter maps HTTP 5xx/429 to IngestError::Unreachable and other non-2xx (incl. 3xx) to BadResponse with redirects never followed. A skip deletes nothing and persists nothing, so the author is retried next pass. A failing fallback is isolated like any other source (source_skipped with fallback_used and fallback_failure).
criteria: One PDS being down skips only that author; the others are indexed and the pass exits 0 (IPF-10)
Down / 503 / 429 skip as pds_unreachable; 404 / non-JSON / redirect skip as listing_failed; a redirect target is never contacted (IPF-11)
classify_fetch_failure maps all 8 failure cases to exactly one documented reason (CORE-12)
A skipped author's earlier claims stay searchable (IPF-14); a skipped author is retried and indexed on the next pass with nothing about the skip persisted (IPF-17)
A failing fallback skips only the affected author with fallback_used true and a fallback_failure reason (IPF-07)

phases.name: Hardening: bounded fan-out, SSRF guard, typed config, self-attested search label
phases.description: Bound the pass (4 concurrent, 30 s per DID, exit 3 on total outage), refuse private/loopback/link-local/ULA PDS addresses after DNS (https only; loopback seam test-only and refused in release builds), validate configuration at startup, and label self-attested claims in openlore search (including contributor search for self-attested authors).

steps.name: Bounded fan-out, one deadline per DID, exit 3 on total outage
steps.description: Fetch phase uses futures-util buffered(max_concurrent_fetches) (default 4) and a single tokio::time::timeout_at deadline per DID (default 30 s) covering both resolving and listing; the pure core sees only FetchFailure::TimedOut{stage} / ResolutionFailure::TimedOut. summarize + pass_exit_code give exit 3 iff at least one DID is configured and every configured DID is skipped, emitted after pass_summary.
criteria: A hanging PDS is skipped as pds_timeout within the per-DID budget and the pass completes (IPF-15)
A DID document that never arrives counts against the same per-DID budget (IPF-16)
With 40 authors, requests in flight never exceed the concurrency cap (IPF-18)
When every author's source fails, pass_summary is the last event and the pass exits 3; earlier claims remain (IPF-19)
Property: own + fallback + skipped == configured, and exit 3 iff configured >= 1 and own + fallback == 0 (CORE-4)

steps.name: SSRF guard: refuse private/loopback/link-local/ULA addresses after DNS, https only
steps.description: ports::net_policy (pure): address_refused(IpAddr) over the documented ranges incl. IPv4-mapped IPv6, and TransportPolicy {HttpsPublicOnly, AllowLoopbackHttp}. pds_endpoint_admissible pre-check (scheme + IP-literal hosts) -> Skip(PdsAddressRefused) without contacting. Guarded constructors AtProtoIngestAdapter::guarded / IdentityLookup::guarded build reqwest clients with a DNS resolver that drops refused addresses (connection goes to the checked IP: rebinding-safe), redirects disabled; refusal = IngestError::AddressRefused. The indexer wires only guarded clients (xtask rule indexer_guarded_clients_only). Policy defaults to HttpsPublicOnly; OPENLORE_INDEXER_ALLOW_LOOPBACK_HTTP=1 selects AllowLoopbackHttp in debug builds only.
criteria: A DID document pointing at a private or insecure address is never followed: the author is skipped as pds_address_refused, the address is never contacted, and the fallback is not used (IPF-20)
A fallback whose name resolves only to a private address is never contacted (IPF-08)
Property: address_refused refuses exactly the documented ranges (CORE-5) and holds at every range edge, e.g. 172.15.255.255 admitted / 172.16.0.0 refused (CORE-13)
Property: pds_endpoint_admissible admits https public endpoints, and loopback http only under the test policy (CORE-6)
